newsitem.title: USA: Exxon profits rise, Amoco falls, Amerada plunges.
newsitem.headline: Exxon profits rise, Amoco falls, Amerada plunges.

text.p: Exxon Corp. reported a 15 percent rise in first-quarter profits Monday, topping Wall Street's expectations, as strong gains in oil and natural gas prices helped to boost profits.

Amoco Corp. said it earnings fell, but the numbers were stacked against a tough quarter last year when a one-time gain boosted profits. The company also was hit by heavy maintenance work on its refineries in the first quarter.
Amerada Hess Corp. said its earnings shrank to less than $5 million from $66 million due to a change in accounting practices.

Exxon, the nation's largest oil company, said it earned $2.17 billion, or 87 cents a share, in the first three months of the year, up from $1.88 billion, or 76 cents a share, a year ago. Analysts had been looking for income of 83 cents per share, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street estimates.
Revenues rose to $33.59 billion from $31.20 billion.
After gaining more than $2 initially, Exxon's stock closed down 12.5 cents at $53.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The earnings showed very strong fundamentals, in particular in the upstream (exploration and production)," said Paul Ting, an analyst at Salomon Brothers.
Exxon, which is based in Irving, Texas, said all of its units did better than a year ago and its earnings, excluding non-recurring items, were the highest quarterly total in the company's history.

"Crude oil and natural gas prices were stronger on average than the prior year, although they weakened during the quarter," Chairman Lee Raymond said in a statement. "Petroleum product sales increased in all major geographic areas to the highest first-quarter level since 1980," he added.
Crude oil prices averaged $3 higher than a year ago.

U.S. exploration and production earnings rose to $554 million from $419 million, despite lower production volumes, while overseas profits were $890 million vs. $1 billion, which included a one-time credit of $125 million.
U.S. refining and marketing turned around to a $57 million profit from a $16 million loss a year ago. Overseas refining and marketing income rose to $297 million from $190 million.
"Overseas refining provided the real surprise," said PaineWebber analyst Steven Pfeiffer.

Chicago-based Amoco said it earned $674 million or $1.36 a share on revenues of $9 billion. A year earlier it earned $728 million or $1.47 a share on revenues of $8.21 billion. The company said that excluding a one-time gain, the year-ago earnings also were $1.36 a share.
"Amoco's performance remains strong at a time when markets for some of our downstream products are relatively weak," said Chief Executive Laurance Fuller.
Amoco said earnings from U.S. exploration and production rose to $365 million from $281 million, but refinery maintenance cut $50 million to $60 million off the profits.
"They were caught in a double whammy, there was downtime on their refineries at the same time as margins on products were improving," said Fadel Gheit, analyst at Fahenstock & Co.
Gheit noted that chemicals earnings at both Exxon and Amoco were markedly higher than the fourth quarter of 1996.
Exxon's chemical division reported sales rose 5 percent and worlwide earnings rose to $310 million from $287 million a year ago and $265 million in the fourth quarter of 1996.

At Amoco, chemicals earnings were below the year ago level of $240 million, but at $147 million were better than the $105 million of the fourth quarter of 1996. Overseas exploration and production operations earned $127 million vs. $121 million a year ago.
Amoco's stock closed up 62.5 cents at $82 on the NYSE.
Meanwhile, Amerada Hess said its first quarter earnings slumped to $4.6 million or 5 cents a share from $66.0 million or 71 cents a share. Revenues rose to $2.41 billion from $2.23 billion.
The New York-based company blamed the sharp drop in earnings on its switch to so-called first in/first out inventory accounting practice.

The accounting change impacted the company's inventory of 40 million barrels in oil products, resulting in a $56 million loss for its refining, marketing and shipping operations compared with a $44 million profit in the year ago quarter.
Amerada's stock closed up 37.5 cents at $49.125 on the NYSE.
